Start on one computer with Python **3.12 or 3.13**, a fresh environment and the
Python tools for your chosen backend. Install the native Palace or AEDT solver
separately before running a calculation. If you later use a remote solver host,
the [portable handoff lesson](execute.qmd) explains that workflow.

## Create a fresh environment

Select the SCGSim source revision recorded for the documentation version you
are using; the version selector and page footer identify that captured
revision. Check out that source before creating the environment and
installing. The general example below uses stable `main`; use the versioned
checkout for version-specific workflows.

```bash
git clone --branch main https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim.git
cd scgsim
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]'
```

Choose extras for the work you want to do:

::: {.table-responsive}

| Work on this computer | Installation from the matching checkout | What it supplies |
|---|---|---|
| Resolve and plot returned results | `pip install -e .` | SCGSim, NumPy and Plotly |
| Prepare Palace geometry/mesh/config | `pip install -e '.[palace]'` | GDSFactory 9.x, GDS reader and Gmsh |
| Prepare ordinary HFSS or Q3D; use Q2D | `pip install -e '.[aedt]'` | GDS reader and PyAEDT 1.3.0 |
| Prepare source-first AEDT Surface EPR | `pip install -e '.[aedt-epr]'` | AEDT dependencies plus GDSFactory 9.x and KLayout 0.30.x |
| Inspect solver-bound geometry | `pip install -e '.[visualization]'` | Mesh reader, image tools and PyVista; combine with the backend extra |

:::

Combine visualization with a backend using, for example,
`pip install -e '.[palace,visualization]'`. For native geometry rendering, use
a computer with a working OpenGL/EGL context; the
[preview reference](../geometry-preview.qmd) describes the available modes.

## Use the public model inputs

The beginner lessons use the public SimplePad component and executable
notebooks from [OrPen SC PDK revision `51985d9`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9).
Install that PDK with SCGSim in the same environment and dependency resolution,
so their shared GDSFactory, kfactory and KLayout versions agree. From the
SCGSim checkout, this command supplies both beginner backend paths and the
notebook kernel tools:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace,aedt-epr,visualization]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk.git@51985d9507025e8241205712e866c0b804de29b9' ipykernel
```

### Select the curved source cell

Keep the `51985d9` pin above for the SimplePad beginner notebooks and use a
separate environment for the curved-source study. The current OrPen SC PDK
teaching revision is
[`ecc9062`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/tree/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52).
It contains the current Circular Pad source lesson, its derived executable
notebook, and public Fresh08 result figures and tables: [source
QMD](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/src/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.qmd),
[IPYNB](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/palace_eigenmode.ipynb),
and [evidence](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk/blob/ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52/notebooks/ComponentSimulation/CircularPad/evidence/README.md).
The QMD is the source authority; the IPYNB is derived from it. Fresh08 used
the earlier OrPen `c79b91e` producer export; exact execution provenance is in
the linked result lesson.

The curved-source APIs used here are available in the SCGSim public develop
revision `2eed1eb` (`1.1.0rc1`); stable `1.0.2` does not include them. For a
released documentation version, use the SCGSim source revision captured for
that version by the selector/footer above. From the root of the selected
checkout, create this separate environment. OrPen does not install SCGSim as
a pip dependency; its `uv` notebook group and lock select SCGSim revision
`2eed1eb` for OrPen's own workflow. This pip command explicitly installs
SCGSim from the selected checkout and OrPen at the current teaching revision:

```bash
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e '.[palace,visualization]' \
  'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk.git@ecc90623b62e55f95afaa5a1f1048a71f81cae52' \
  ipykernel
```

::: {.callout-note title="Select the current development source" collapse="true"}
The current public SCGSim development source is commit
[`2eed1eb`](https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim/tree/2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71)
(package version `1.1.0rc1`, an installable develop revision rather than a
stable release). Select this exact source for a development reproduction
before creating the curved-study environment:

```bash
git clone --branch develop https://github.com/OrPenStrike/scgsim.git scgsim-development
cd scgsim-development
git switch --detach 2eed1eb4a9bcc7b1b020feb4953d5ed27e7d7b71
```

Then run the curved-study install command above. This is an optional
development source, not the default for version-selected installation.
:::

::: {#native-palace-for-this-curved-uniform-port .callout-note title="Native Palace for this curved Uniform port"}
Use a native Palace executable built from [revision
`4e9e1b7`](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/tree/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37),
or a descendant containing the [curved-port extent correction](https://github.com/arfiligol/palace/blob/4e9e1b7232b4c8ca8b964be7e70f1848f578de37/palace/utils/geodata_impl.cpp).
The SCGSim Python extra above does not install or update the native Palace
executable. Configure this study to use that executable or a wrapper that
invokes it. This prerequisite is specific to this curved Uniform-port
example, not ordinary Palace geometry preparation or AEDT workflows.
:::

Open the linked IPYNB in your notebook frontend and select this checkout's
`.venv` kernel, using `.venv/bin/python`. Its default `analyze_handoff` action
reads a retained `.artifacts` run tree, which is not included with the public
source and figures. To prepare or execute your own run, select
`prepare_handoff` or `run` in the notebook and choose a fresh run ID; `run`
uses the separately installed native Palace executable described above.

The current Fresh08 result reports mode 1 at 5.573354161115 GHz after four
refinements and five solve/estimate snapshots. Its final native indicator
0.1186681863426 remains above the configured 0.02; the native run/log also
recorded PCG warnings. These observations do not establish mesh convergence or numerical
accuracy. The
[Palace lesson](palace-eigenmode.qmd#circular-pad-lc-study) shows the result
and its limits.

Check which SCGSim version you installed:

```python
from importlib.metadata import version
print(version("scgsim"))
```

Keep that version and the model's source revision with your study notes.

::: {.callout-note title="Installing the deeper Xmon example" collapse="true"}
The deeper Xmon lesson uses a separate PDK revision. When following it, install
its pinned inputs and the appropriate SCGSim extra together:

```bash
python -m pip install -e '.[palace]' 'orpen-sc-pdk @ git+https://github.com/OrPenStrike/orpen-sc-pdk.git@35b4dc1cdd3f921badcac2fe57a98366315ae8d9'
```

Keep the PDK revision matched to the example you run.
:::

## Prepare the solver host separately

For Palace, make your executable or wrapper available and configure the
launch resources and setup commands for your computer. SCGSim generates the
local or selected Slurm launch script; Palace itself is installed separately.

For AEDT, use **AEDT 2024.2**, **PyAEDT 1.3.0** and an appropriate license.
The generated script starts its Desktop session, saves the project and
releases the session. Reading returned results later does not require opening
Desktop.

Next [extract a pad capacitance](../tutorials/capacitance.qmd) or
[find a resonance and read EPR](../tutorials/resonance-epr.qmd). If you already
have a returned package, start with [reading results](returned-results.qmd).
